key_highlights: RBA issued a blunt hawkish warning ahead of its next rate decision, with IMF separately urging spending cuts as another hike looms (#41, #74)
ASX closed a volatile week with modest gains as oil prices and bond yields eased; big four banks led advances (#50, #68)
Iron ore prices under pressure ('roaches seethe'), weighing on BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX sentiment (#51)
Recession odds for 2027 rising amid sticky inflation, petrol price shock, and housing unaffordability (#48, #55, #56)
Japan diverting Australian LNG exports while East Coast gas supply tightens, pressuring energy sector (#52)
Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, a structural positive for QLD infrastructure and tech (#77)
Qantas ground staff strike threat over Joyce-era bargaining agreements adds operational risk to QAN.AX (#63)
Gold sector catalysts: Forrestania four WA prefeasibility studies and Aurum Côte d'Ivoire high-grade discovery (#38, #47)
Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman at 96, a generational shift in global value investing (#19)
Bendigo Bank (BEN.AX) job cuts concentrated in Adelaide; Coles (COL.AX) maintains elevated milk prices despite axing farmer support (#22, #66)

sectors.trend: Iron ore weakness persists; copper recovery contract to China's NERIN signals continued China demand but at lower margins. Gold sector sees multiple prefeasibility catalysts.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from soft iron ore. Gold names (WPM.AX, NGN.AX, GWN.AX) benefit from safe-haven flows and new project pipelines. KCM's $498m NERIN contract supports copper midstream.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advanced on the day as yields eased, but RBA hawkishness and IMF spending warnings cap upside. Bendigo Bank restructuring signals stress in regional banking.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher NIMs but face credit-risk concerns if recession materialises. BEN.AX under pressure from Adelaide job cuts. Superannuation system reform debate (#17) could reshape fund flows.

sectors.trend: LNG export diversion to Japan tightens domestic East Coast gas supply. Petrol price shock adds to inflation. Victoria retreats from renewable transmission, favouring coal pathway.
sectors.implications: SOL.AX, WDS.AX, GWO.AX face domestic supply constraints. Coal re-emergence (#73) supports BHP.AX thermal coal and AWE.AX. Petrol shock (#55) pressures consumer discretionary and transport costs.

sectors.trend: Coles maintains elevated milk prices; housing unaffordability at extreme levels; tenants see modest relief. Qantas strike threat disrupts travel.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, COL.AX face margin pressure from input costs. REITs (GPW.AX, SPG.AX) pressured by unaffordable housing and tenant relief dynamics. QAN.AX faces strike risk.

sectors.trend: Anthropic's $31bn QLD datacentre is a landmark AI infrastructure investment. ASX small-caps (Latrobe, CurveBeam, Arrow, Sultan) show relative strength.
sectors.implications: Structural tailwind for QLD-based infrastructure and datacentre plays. Small-cap momentum in ASX200 laggards suggests rotation. AI adoption narrative supports CSL.AX diagnostics and tech-adjacent names.

sectors.trend: No major ASX-specific catalysts today; global pharma (TMO) positioned for resurgence per US headlines.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains a defensive anchor; global biotech sentiment neutral-to-positive. No immediate ASX healthcare catalysts.

key_themes: RBA hawkish pivot and potential further rate hikes amid sticky inflation
Iron ore and LNG export dynamics weighing on commodity exporters
Housing unaffordability and petrol shock as domestic inflation drivers
AI infrastructure investment (Anthropic QLD) as long-term structural theme
Generational leadership shift with Buffett's departure from Berkshire
Immigration policy tightening impacting regional labour supply
Middle East oil shock risk as a tail-risk scenario

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike / IMF fiscal tightening
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight financials (NIM expansion) and short-duration bonds; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and property developers
Maintain defensive allocation to CSL.AX, WES.AX; reduce exposure to cyclicals (FMG.AX, QAN.AX); hold cash buffer
Underweight BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into gold (WPM.AX, NGN.AX) and copper midstream

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil shock / LNG supply disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; monitor SOL.AX, WDS.AX for domestic gas price spikes; consider energy hedges
Reduce QAN.AX exposure pre-strike; monitor Qantas bargaining outcomes
Underweight property developers and REITs; monitor NAB.AX, ANZ.AX mortgage arrears data

defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore 'roaches seethe'; China demand soft; recession risk amplifies commodity downside

defensive_moves.rationale: Housing unaffordability at extreme levels; RBA hikes pressure valuations; tenant relief limits rental growth

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% cash allocation as recession odds rise
defensive_moves.rationale: 2027 recession probability increasing; IMF fiscal warning; RBA hawkish; preserve dry powder

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound and volatile. RBA rate decision is the dominant catalyst. Banks and gold may outperform; materials and REITs lag. Petrol shock and Qantas strike add near-term noise. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a tight band with elevated VIX.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Rising 2027 recession odds, IMF fiscal tightening, and housing stress cap cyclicals. Structural positives in AI infrastructure (Anthropic QLD), gold pipeline, and bank NIMs provide selective opportunities. A soft-landing scenario remains base case but probability is declining.
